name: node-emoji-random-key-renamed-to-name-muenchhausen
behavioral_change: node-emoji v2.0.0 rewrote the codebase and changed the field names of the object returned by `emoji.random()`. In v_old (1.10.0) it returned `{ key, emoji }`; in v_new (2.2.0) it returns `{ emoji, name }`, so reading `.key` yields undefined without any exception or warning.
downstream_effect: The downstream project's `Emoji.prototype.random` in lib/fake/emoji/index.js maps `res.key` to `result.value`, which becomes undefined after the upgrade while `result.text` still works. The single failure is a should assertion ("expected 'undefined' to be equals one of Array [...]") from a reflection-generated test with frames only in should internals and test/fake-functions-interface-validation.js:28; node-emoji, the edited file, res.key and res.name never appear.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in lib/fake/emoji/index.js:19 from `value : res.key` to `value : res.name`.
documented_in: The node-emoji 2.2.0 README section `### emoji.random()` shows the example output `// { name: 'unicorn', emoji: '🦄' }`, and the 1.10.0 README shows `{ emoji: '❤️', key: 'heart' }`; the rename is not announced in any changelog or migration guide (the v2.0.2 release notes mention only a new codebase, ESM support and a `replace` change), so the new form must be inferred by comparing the two READMEs.
failing_tests: test/fake-functions-interface-validation.js :: Validate fake methods > Emoji.random > Emoji.random function should have property .value
test_cmd: npm run eslint && npm run mocha
